metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% above peak for next 3–7 days.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-period, model delays correction; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next 2–5 days.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in early forecast horizon (1–3 days) — if price drops >3% from recent peak, forecast should not rise above 1% above prior low.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model overfits recent volatility; use 3–5 day moving average as baseline for next 7–14 days.
- If true outcome shows rapid decline after 10–15 days of high prices, model often fails to anticipate; add 1–2% downward bias for next 5–7 days.
- Model underestimates downward momentum when sentiment is negative and price is above 45.00; apply 1–3% downward adjustment for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history shows 3+ consecutive negative entries, model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.
